subject: Pricing exhibit — escrow mitigation / stabilization language clarification
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@oceana.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on Pricing Exhibit — escrow/smoothing language

Hi Stephanie / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. We dug into the pricing exhibit and have a couple of items we need clarified before we can sign: the escrow waterfall and the proposed floor/cap true-up mechanics. Specifically:

- Section 2.3 (Escrow & Stabilization): the way the waterfall is written, an overage in Month M can be clawed back across the following 12 months. For our business (seasonal peaks), that creates cashflow volatility — can we limit the clawback to a 6-month window for spikes originating in the onboarding quarter?

- Section 4 (Minimum / Floor): if we fall below the stated floor in a quarter due to a one-off vendor outage, we'd like a temporary graceband so we aren't assessed full remediation charges immediately. Proposal: temporary crediting (up to 30% of the delta) for the first two months after a verified outage.

- Related ask: can you add a 60-day notice for any unilateral fee rollback or change to the floor? We need time to plan operationally.

I attached a short doc with our suggested edits (Oceana_Pricing_Requested_Amendments.pdf) and highlighted the sections above.

We'd prefer to avoid heavy legal redlines at this stage — hoping for a pragmatic commercial patch we can sign quickly. Can you review with finance / legal and let me know what is feasible?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Vendor Ops
Oceana Logistics

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on Pricing Exhibit — escrow/smoothing language

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and the attachment.

We hear the ask: limit the clawback window for seasonal spikes, a short graceband for outage-driven dips, and a 60-day notice for fee rollbacks. I looped in Ben (finance) and Marissa (legal/sales ops) to weigh in on commercial feasibility and draft language.

Quick clarifying Qs before we draft a proposal:
- Is the 6-month clawback window requested only for spikes that originate during your onboarding quarter (first 90 days), or for any seasonal spike?
- For the outage graceband, do you want credits applied as a percent of the delta or as a dollar cap per event?

We'll produce a short commercial amendment (one page) that we can attach to the order schedule if we land on the mechanics. If possible, please confirm the answers above by EOD Friday so we can move quickly.

Proposed next step: Ben will run a quick model of the cashflow impact (sheet attached when available) and we can propose language that ties to verified incident windows.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@oceana.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2027 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on Pricing Exhibit — escrow/smoothing language

Elena / team — thanks, this is helpful context. I ran a few scenarios against the commit bands and wanted to propose an alternative that keeps the commercial intent but reduces accounting/cashflow friction for both sides.

High-level proposal (commercial, not legal text):
1) Stabilization Credit Pool: instead of a straight clawback over 12 months, Redwood would hold a small stabilization credit pool equal to 4% of the quarter's billed amount. When verified spikes occur (per the incident verification process in Exhibit D), up to 50% of the pool can be used to offset overage charges for up to 6 months. Any unused portion of the pool rolls forward into the next quarter and is reconciled at annual true-up.

2) Outage Graceband: for outage-driven underutilization, Redwood would apply a temporary credit equal to 30% of the quarterly delta for the first two months post-incident, capped at $50K per incident. Credits apply only after validation by our incident review team.

3) Change management / rollback notice: 60-day notice for fee changes as requested. For material pricing changes (>=5% effective unit price), Redwood agrees a joint operational plan must be shared 90 days prior.

Attached is the model I used (escrow-model-v3.xlsx) — it includes examples for a 6-month window vs 12-month and shows cashflow and carry-forward impacts.

If that approach is acceptable commercially, Marissa and Stephanie will draft a one-page amendment with the minimal legal language and we'll push to a quick signature cycle.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
attachment: escrow-model-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@oceana.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on Pricing Exhibit — escrow/smoothing language

Thanks — that structure is much closer to what we had in mind and addresses our cashflow concern. Two final points before we sign:

- We accept the Stabilization Credit Pool concept with the parameters you proposed, but request explicit language that the pool calculation is based on "billed amount" (post-credit) not gross committed spend.
- Please add a 60-day notice for rollback and confirm the 90-day plan requirement only applies for >=5% material pricing changes.

If you can include those clarifications in the one-page amendment (and the DocuSign link), we can route internally and aim to sign by the end of next week.

Also: please include a short clause that any credits applied due to verified incidents are applied within the next invoice cycle (no more than 45 days after validation).

Thanks again for moving quickly on this — attaching our marked PDF for reference.

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, Vendor Ops
Oceana Logistics
